seo.title: Hermes Agent vs HagiCode: Features and Comparison
seo.description: Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source, self-improving agent; HagiCode runs it as a coding executor. Compare features, pricing, setup and fit.

summary: Hermes Agent is Nous Research's open-source agent with memory, skills, scheduling and chat gateways, and HagiCode is a workbench that runs Hermes as a coding executor over ACP. Use Hermes alone as an always-on assistant; add HagiCode for parallel coding sessions, proposals and commits.

content: Hermes Agent is an open-source, self-improving agent from Nous Research. You run `hermes` in a terminal, or reach it from Telegram, Discord, Slack and other chat apps, and it keeps memory and builds skills over time. HagiCode is a desktop and web AI programming workbench that drives agent CLIs, Hermes among them, as its executor. It does not replace Hermes; it runs `hermes acp` inside a repository and adds sessions, proposals and commit handling.

Hermes is broader than a coding agent, and that matters here. If you want an always-on assistant, scheduled jobs or a bot in your chat apps, stay with Hermes alone: HagiCode uses its ACP mode, where Hermes' own docs say messaging delivery and cron management are excluded. If your goal is coding work across repositories, HagiCode is the layer that organises it.

sections.title: Hermes Agent vs HagiCode at a glance

cells: What it is
Open-source self-improving agent with memory, skills, scheduler and chat gateway; coding is one use
Workbench that runs agent CLIs, Hermes included, as coding executors
Interface and platforms
Terminal UI; Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Email; Linux, macOS, WSL2, native Windows, Termux; desktop app on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows
Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux), Docker Compose container, Microsoft Store edition
Pricing and licensing
MIT-licensed and free; you pay your model provider, or an optional Nous Portal subscription
Desktop and Container free; Store edition free with optional one-time TurboEngine purchase
Model and provider access
Nous Portal (300+ models), OpenRouter, OpenAI, your own endpoint and more; switch with `hermes model`
Hosts no models; uses what Hermes is configured with; optional OmniRoute routing
Parallel work
Spawns isolated sub-agents; seven terminal backends including Docker, SSH, Modal and Daytona
Several sessions at once, each a named Agent with visible status
Spec and planning workflow
No proposal workflow; learns reusable skills from experience
OpenSpec proposals: propose, validate, apply, archive (3 concurrent free, 32 with TurboEngine)
Git and commit handling
Works through its terminal tools; the README documents no dedicated commit workflow
AI-composed commit messages with the repository locked during the commit; Git and GitHub integration
Setup effort
One-line installer that builds its own Python environment, then `hermes setup`
Desktop install, plus Hermes installed with its ACP support and a provider configured
Best for
An always-on personal or team agent across terminal, chat and cron jobs
Coding work across repositories with parallel sessions and traceable specs

items.title: A learning loop and long-term memory
content: Hermes creates skills after complex tasks, improves them as it uses them, searches its own past conversations with full-text search and LLM summaries, and builds a model of you across sessions. It follows the agentskills.io open standard, so skills are portable. This is the feature to choose Hermes for.

items.title: It lives where you do
content: One gateway process connects Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and the CLI, with voice-memo transcription. A built-in cron scheduler takes natural-language jobs, such as nightly backups or weekly audits, and delivers results to any connected platform.

items.title: Runs anywhere, not just a laptop
content: Hermes supports seven terminal backends: local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona and Vercel Sandbox. Daytona and Modal can hibernate when idle, so you can run it on a small VPS and talk to it from chat while it works on a cloud machine.

items.title: Model freedom and delegation
content: `hermes model` switches provider and model without code changes; the Nous Portal subscription is optional and bundles models with web search, image generation and a cloud browser. Hermes can spawn isolated sub-agents and write scripts that call its tools over RPC. Releases are frequent and still 0.x (v0.22 in October 2026).

sections.title: When to choose Hermes Agent, and when to choose HagiCode

items: you want an always-on assistant you can message from Telegram, Discord or Slack;
you want scheduled, unattended jobs delivered to a chat platform;
you want the agent on a VPS or serverless sandbox instead of your laptop;
you value Hermes' memory, skills that improve with use, and cross-session recall;
you want to switch providers with `hermes model` and optionally use Nous Portal.
you do coding work and want several Hermes sessions at once, each tracked as a named Agent;
you want each change to start as a written OpenSpec proposal with validation and archive;
you want Hermes' code changes committed with AI-written messages and fixed in an embedded editor;
you also use Claude Code, Codex or other agent CLIs and want one workspace for all of them;
you want Hermes' research and findings kept in a shared Vault, with Monospecs covering several repositories.

blocks.title: Where HagiCode is not the right tool for Hermes users
content: Messaging, cron and always-on use: HagiCode runs Hermes in ACP mode, where Hermes' docs exclude messaging delivery and cron management, so run Hermes directly for those.
Headless CI or scripted runs: call `hermes` directly; HagiCode is a desktop and web app.
It needs Hermes installed with ACP support and a provider configured first, so setup is longer than running Hermes alone.
HagiCode requests Hermes' `bypassPermissions` ACP mode by default; review your Hermes approval settings and work in a repository you can restore.
Free editions cap concurrent proposals at 3, and teams that do not want spec discipline will find proposals overhead.
HagiCode is not an IDE replacement for deep manual editing beyond the embedded Code Server.

sections.title: Using Hermes Agent together with HagiCode

content: HagiCode is a workbench on top of the CLI. It starts `hermes acp` in the repository you open, so your own Hermes install and provider credentials do the work. Hermes keeps reading its provider setup from its own configuration, `~/.hermes/.env` or `config.yaml`.
Nothing is locked in: Hermes stays a normal install, with its memory, skills and gateway untouched.

items: Install Hermes (Linux, macOS, WSL2: `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash`; Windows PowerShell: `iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)`).
Run `hermes setup` or `hermes model` to choose a provider, then check ACP with `hermes acp --check`; the ACP support may need its extra installed, as the Hermes ACP docs describe.
Install HagiCode Desktop (Windows, macOS or Linux; free) and choose Hermes as the Agent CLI, optionally setting a model.
Open a repository and start a session or an OpenSpec proposal.
Expect Hermes to run its coding tools in that repository; its chat gateway and scheduler are not part of the session.
To go back to plain Hermes, run `hermes` directly; nothing in your Hermes setup changed.

blocks.title: What works for Hermes inside HagiCode
content: Parallel sessions, Agents management, OpenSpec proposals, AI commit, Code Server, Monospecs, Vault and the unified tool-call view apply to Hermes sessions. OmniRoute is a HagiCode feature, and how far it reaches Hermes depends on Hermes' own provider settings.
Interactive questions are limited to Claude, Pi, OMP and Reasonix, and the agent work panel is Claude only, so neither is available with Hermes.

sections.title: What HagiCode adds on top of any agent

items.title: Parallel sessions and Agents management
content: Hermes can spawn sub-agents inside one conversation. HagiCode adds the level above: several Hermes sessions across tasks or repositories, each a named Agent whose status you can see.

items.title: OpenSpec proposals
content: Hermes learns from experience, but its memory is not a record of why a change was made. An OpenSpec proposal is: the problem, the agreed approach and the resulting code changes stay together and can be archived.

items.title: AI commit and Code Server
content: HagiCode drafts the commit message from the diff and locks the repository during the commit. Code Server opens the files Hermes changed in a browser editor, so review and edits stay in one window.

items.title: Monospecs and Vault
content: Monospecs declares sub-repositories in `.hagicode/monospecs.yaml` so a cross-repo change reaches Hermes as one proposal. Vault holds reference projects and notes shared across projects, next to what Hermes remembers about you.

items.title: OmniRoute, tool-call view and usage
content: OmniRoute can centralise model routing across agents. Hermes tool calls appear in the same typed view as every other agent's, and optional TokenMonitor shows today's tokens and cost in the status bar.

items: Hermes Agent is a broad, self-improving agent that also codes; HagiCode is a coding workbench that can run it.
HagiCode adds parallel Agents, proposals, AI commits and a knowledge base around Hermes' coding use, but not its chat gateway or scheduler.
Use Hermes alone for an always-on assistant, and HagiCode plus Hermes for organised, multi-repository coding.

faq.question: Is Hermes Agent free?
faq.answer: Hermes Agent is MIT-licensed and free to install. You pay your model provider, or optionally a Nous Portal subscription that bundles models and tools; see portal.nousresearch.com for current plans.

faq.question: How do I install Hermes Agent?
faq.answer: On Linux, macOS or WSL2 run `curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash`. On native Windows run `iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)` in PowerShell, then start it with `hermes`.

faq.question: Can I use Hermes Agent with HagiCode?
faq.answer: Yes. Install Hermes and configure a provider, then choose Hermes as the Agent CLI in HagiCode. HagiCode runs `hermes acp` in your repository.

faq.question: Does HagiCode replace Hermes Agent?
faq.answer: No. Hermes does the work; HagiCode organises sessions, proposals and commits around it. Its chat gateway and scheduler are not available inside HagiCode sessions.

faq.question: Is Hermes Agent a coding agent?
faq.answer: It can code, but it is a general agent first, with memory, skills, scheduled jobs and chat gateways. HagiCode uses its coding side.

faq.question: Hermes vs HagiCode: which should I pick?
faq.answer: Pick Hermes alone for an always-on, multi-platform assistant. Add HagiCode when the job is coding across repositories and you want parallel sessions, proposals and managed commits.
